aliases: fries with cheese curds and gravy

winner.title: The Ultimate Poutine

evidence.authenticity: Classic trio: twice-fried russet fries, fresh squeaky white cheddar curds at room temperature, roux-based beef gravy. Author is not Canadian, but the dish is made traditionally.
evidence.precision: Volumes plus produce sizing (4 large russets, about 2 lb, 1/4-inch sticks); 4 temperatures (350F, 425F); 10 sensory cues (golden blonde roux, reduced to 2 cups, pale blonde, deep golden brown); Dutch oven or wok named but no inches.
evidence.testing: Serious Eats test kitchen. Explains fresh curds (under 24 hours), gravy balance, soak and freezing-step note for crispier fries. Only 2 ratings, though.
evidence.photos: 5 of 5 steps have images in schema (gravy, soak, both fries, assembly).
evidence.efficiency: Stated total 1 hr 40 min, mostly the 1 hour potato soak; gravy can be made during the soak. Needs homemade pressure-cooker beef stock (see note), which adds time.
evidence.access: Fresh cheese curds are the only hard item (some US grocers, cheese shops, or homemade). Beef stock and peanut oil are easy.

winner.why: Beat the NYT version on step photos, explicit frying temperatures, and a more traditional, simpler gravy.

runnerUp.title: Poutine

evidence.authenticity: Intro explains the rural Quebec roots and the Lachance anecdote; gravy adds ketchup, thyme, and chicken plus beef stock, which are common variations.
evidence.precision: Sizes given (3 lb russets, 1/3-inch planks, 2 to 3 inches of oil); temps 325F and 375F; 13 sensory cues; doneness cues on most steps.
evidence.testing: NYT test process; explains the soak purpose. 119 ratings, average 4.
evidence.photos: No step images in schema; step photos may be hidden by login, so not marked down fully.
evidence.efficiency: About 2.5 hours stated; the soak is 1 hour or more.
evidence.access: Cheese curds are needed; the recipe has a tip on them.

runnerUp.why: Strong and well-rated, but a more elaborate gravy and fewer visible photos than Serious Eats.

candidates.disqualified: Not disqualified, but scored low: lists mozzarella as an alternative to curds, uses chicken wings in the gravy, and has no step photos.
No ingredient amounts, no temperatures; only a general technique article.

searches: poutine québécoise recette authentique sauce fromage en grains
notes: Fresh cheese curds are the only real sourcing issue in the US. Serious Eats has only 2 ratings, while NYT has 119 at 4.0. The Serious Eats recipe calls for homemade pressure-cooker beef stock, but good store-bought stock would work.
